description: Single-panel "banana" scatter diagram (Ashby-style property map) for Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys, plotting total elongation TE (%) on the y-axis (0-100, ticks every 10) against ultimate tensile strength UTS (MPa) on the x-axis (0-1800, ticks every 200). A secondary top axis labelled (GPa%) marks 10, 30, 50 and 70 and is crossed by dashed hyperbolic iso-contours of constant UTS×TE (strength-ductility product). Data points use many marker symbols (filled triangles, diamonds, squares, circles, plus signs, crosses, open squares/circles) distributed as clouds, but no legend keys markers to specific alloys. Overlaid outlined fields label alloy families: a green ellipse "δ single phase" (TE below ~40%, UTS ~200-800 MPa) that encloses the conventional-steel labels BH, CMn, TRIP, DP/CP and HSLA; an unshaded top-left field with Mild, IF and IF-HS; a light-blue ellipse "γ single phase" (TE ~50-100%, UTS ~700-1250 MPa) holding the highest TE points; a large ellipse "Mn-TWIP" overlapping it; a pink-square "δ based duplex" field; a "γ based duplex" field (TE ~15-60%, UTS ~600-1100 MPa) inside an outer dark dashed boundary; and a bottom-right dashed ellipse "γ+(δ)+coarse κ" with the label MS, at TE below ~20% and UTS ~1000-1800 MPa. The figure demonstrates that strength-ductility combinations separate according to matrix phase and to the presence of coarse κ-carbide.

observations.observation: The x-axis is labelled UTS (MPa) and spans 0-1800 with ticks every 200 MPa; the y-axis is labelled TE (%) and spans 0-100 with ticks every 10%.
A secondary top axis labelled (GPa%) carries the tick values 10, 30, 50 and 70, crossed by dashed hyperbolic iso-contour curves, i.e. lines of constant UTS×TE.

A green outlined ellipse labelled 'δ single phase' covers roughly UTS 200-800 MPa and TE up to about 40%, and encloses the conventional-steel class labels BH, CMn, TRIP, DP/CP and HSLA printed in green text.
A light-blue ellipse labelled 'γ single phase' occupies about UTS 700-1250 MPa and TE 50-100%, containing the highest-elongation points (filled triangles near TE ~95%) among all fields.
A large unshaded ellipse labelled 'Mn-TWIP' overlaps the γ single phase field and the γ based duplex field.
A field marked mainly by pink/magenta squares is labelled 'δ based duplex' and lies at roughly TE 25-65% and UTS 500-1000 MPa.
A field labelled 'γ based duplex' lies at about TE 15-60% and UTS 600-1100 MPa and is enclosed by a larger dark dashed boundary ellipse shared with the γ single phase region.

A dashed ellipse at the bottom right is labelled 'γ+(δ)+coarse κ' and is associated with the label MS; it sits at TE below about 20% and UTS about 1000-1800 MPa, i.e. poor elongation at high strength.
An unshaded region at the upper left is annotated 'Mild', 'IF' and 'IF-HS', marking the position of conventional soft steels at low UTS and low TE.
The caption states the figure is TE as a function of UTS in Fe-Mn-Al-C alloys for a uniform specimen geometry corresponding to ASTM E-8 standard (50 mm × 12.5 mm × 1 mm).
The caption states the tensile data were taken from solution-treated and water-quenched strips, citing references [6–9,11,23,37,41,42,51,60–87,118,160].
The citing text states that the tensile properties were measured from specimens with tensile direction parallel to the strip rolling direction.

The citing text asserts that ferrite-based duplex steels are located on the upper bound of the first generation advanced high strength steels (1G-AHSS), and that single-phase austenitic steels cover the Mn TWIP steel location but over a larger area.

The citing text asserts that austenite-based duplex steels show lower TE than single-phase austenitic steels at similar strength levels, and that coarse κ-carbides in the austenitic matrix give very poor tensile elongation irrespective of strength.

subfigures.description: Single Ashby-type 'banana' scatter plot: TE (%) vs UTS (MPa) with a top (GPa%) axis and dashed constant UTS×TE iso-contours, overlaid with labelled ellipses/fields for γ single phase, Mn-TWIP, δ based duplex, γ based duplex, δ single phase (BH, CMn, TRIP, DP/CP, HSLA), Mild/IF/IF-HS and γ+(δ)+coarse κ (MS), populated by many marker symbol types without a symbol legend.

unreadable_items: No marker legend is present, so individual data points cannot be assigned to specific alloys/compositions.
Small green labels at the bottom of the δ single phase field (a 'HSS'-like label near UTS ~550-600 MPa) are only partially readable.
Exact boundaries of the hand-drawn field ellipses cannot be read numerically from the plot.
